# Adapter compatibility matrix

Generated evidence for the official AAO adapters under adapter contract v1 and conformance suite v1 ([ADR-025](../decisions/ADR-025-adapter-and-portability-contract.md), [adapter contract](../architecture/adapter-contract.md)). Every "Conformance" cell comes from running the canonical scenarios through `verifyAdapterConformance`. None is typed by hand. "Declared" is what the adapter's manifest claims.

**This matrix is not runtime authority.** It cannot enable an adapter, authorize an actor, or grant a permission. A compatible adapter can still be unauthorized for a Run. Governance, Authorization, the Tool support gate, and Approval decide that.

Conformance dataset: `aao.adapter-conformance@1.0.0`.

## Known limitations

Declared by each manifest. They are informational and never change behavior.

| Adapter | Limitation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aao.native-model` | `reference.semantics_only` | The semantic reference for model conformance, not a provider integration. |
| `aao.vercel-ai-sdk` | `model.provider_injected` | The host injects the language model. The adapter never reads credentials or chooses a provider. |
| `aao.vercel-ai-sdk` | `model.single_invocation` | The SDK's own retries are disabled. AAO invokes exactly once per request, and Runtime reliability policy owns retries. |
| `aao.native-tool` | `reference.semantics_only` | The semantic reference for Tool-provider conformance, not an integration. |
| `aao.mcp-connector` | `tool.execution_id_not_forwarded` | The toolExecutionId is not sent to the server, so execution_id idempotency cannot be asserted. A write_draft MCP Tool is never recovery-safe. |
| `aao.mcp-connector` | `tool.structured_output_required` | A remote result without structured content fails closed. |
| `aao.mcp-connector` | `transport.stdio_only` | One explicit stdio session per server. No HTTP transport, remote authentication flows, resources, prompts, or sampling. |
